clue.text: Furious about doctor providing water

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: furious means very angry
to doctor results is to falsify or rig them

explanation.surface: An angry medic hands out drinks of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun for a physician, but it is the verb meaning to tamper with, and 'providing' just joins the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply it with water through channels, so the verb is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Loud soldiers I come in front of

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
the ego is the self, the 'I'

explanation.surface: A noisy band of troops marches ahead of the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not taken as the letter here: it becomes EGO, the Latin for I and the word for the self.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego, as distinct from forgo, means to precede, literally go before something in time or place.

clue.text: Officer's order requiring assent with day off

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled or gone wrong, so the letters lose their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A commander will only give a command if a day's leave is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day off' reads as a holiday, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on ASSENT and DAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand easy is a parade-ground command allowing soldiers already at ease to relax further, so an officer would shout it.

clue.text: Ran through fence, bandaged by one doctor

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a bandage wraps around a wound, so one piece is wrapped by the other

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
a pale is a stake, or a fence made of stakes

explanation.surface: Someone crashed through a fence and was patched up by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran through' is the definition, not the action at the fence; a pale is an old word for a fence stake, as in 'beyond the pale'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce with a sharp point, so 'ran through' as with a sword or stake matches the past tense.

clue.text: On energy, Greens welcoming right limit

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting one part on another sets it above, so it comes earlier
to welcome a guest is to take them inside, so one piece is let into the other

parts.note: veg, short for vegetables, are greens
R is the abbreviation for right
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An environmental party, fired up on energy policy, embraces a right-wing cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' suggests the political party but means vegetables; VEG takes in R and the result sits on top of E.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is an edge or border, so the point beyond which something cannot go, as in 'on the verge of'.

clue.text: Students and I writing about prejudice

parts.note: a class is a group of students
taken as written

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Pupils and the narrator compose essays about bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the topic of the writing, but it signals the manuscript abbreviation is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Classism is discrimination against people on grounds of social class, one particular kind of bias.

clue.text: Fast runner at the end of a French Open

indicators.note: placing one part at the end of another means it comes after it in the answer

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
Usain Bolt, the Jamaican sprinter

explanation.surface: A sprinter finishes at the end of the French Open tennis tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Open' reads as the tennis tournament at Roland Garros; it splits into 'a French' and the definition 'Open'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbolt a door is to draw back its bolt, allowing it to be swung wide, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Dash or run, filled with life? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: something filled with stuff holds it inside, so one piece sits within another
this reverses the roles just stated, so the outer and inner pieces swap places

parts.note: bio- is the Greek-derived prefix for life, as in biology
R is run, from cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Sprinting or jogging, full of vitality? No, the reverse is true.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, R would be filled with BIO; 'quite the opposite' flips it, so BIO is filled with R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash and brio both mean lively style and verve, vigour shown in a performance or manner.

clue.text: Border where trees still grow entire limb, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one arrangement among many that the letters could take

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: On a mountainside, trees still grow whole branches up to a certain boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is long and descriptive; the last three words carry all the letters. The answer also hides BERLIN, the theme of 27.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber line, or tree line, is the altitude or latitude past which forest stops growing, an edge zone.

clue.text: Complaint about AC/DC, back in Ireland

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one word is placed around another

parts.note: a hernia is a medical complaint

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are written backwards

parts.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to BI

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about the rock band AC/DC once they're home in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC looks like the Australian rock band or electric current, but it is slang for bisexual, which crosswords shorten to two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the classical Latin name for Ireland, still used poetically and in institutional names.

clue.text: Good crew member miserable in protest

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
OS is an ordinary seaman, one of a ship's crew
low means depressed or miserable

explanation.surface: A decent sailor is unhappy about taking part in a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: OS for ordinary seaman is a standard crossword abbreviation for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is industrial action in which workers deliberately reduce their pace, a British form of labour dispute.

clue.text: Save complex remote measuring device

parts.note: save and bar both mean except, as in 'all bar one'

indicators.note: something complex is intricately put together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rescue an intricate gadget that takes readings from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb meaning rescue, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer is an instrument that gauges atmospheric pressure, so a measuring device is a general description of it.

clue.text: American escaping prison traverses empty ditches

indicators.note: whatever is escaping gets out and leaves, so it is removed

parts.note: a jail is a prison
A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A US convict breaks out and crosses dry trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditches' looks like trenches but is the verb: JAIL loses A, then add the outside of 'traverses'.
explanation.definitionFit: To jilt a lover is to abandon them abruptly, and to ditch someone is informal for dumping them.

clue.text: Head of church inclined to accept saint's purification

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which leads off the answer

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: leaning means sloping or inclined
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A church leader is disposed to accept a holy man's ritual purification.
explanation.walkthrough: The church's first letter starts the answer; then the saint's S goes inside LEANING.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansing and purification both name the act of making something clean, physically or spiritually.

clue.text: Art working briefly in dramatic Shakespearean event

parts.note: a temp works short-term placements
'art' is the old form of 'are', a part of the verb to be; est is the Latin and French for 'is'

explanation.surface: An art installation, brief and lively, staged within a Shakespeare performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' looks like painting, but it is the old verb form as in 'thou art'; the setter pairs it with EST, a form of the same verb to be.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tempest is Shakespeare's play, and a tempest is a violent storm, the dramatic event that opens it.

clue.text: Perhaps ideal boost after climbing mountain

indicators.note: one part following another places it later in the answer
in a down answer, climbing means going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
a tonic is a pick-me-up, a boost

explanation.surface: A pick-me-up after scaling a peak might be just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a definition by example: Plato's theory of Forms is the source of the 'Platonic ideal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonic describes things in the realm of Plato's perfect Forms, so an ideal can be one sort of Platonic thing.

clue.text: Atmosphere in the City holding Sri Lankan back

indicators.note: back means the other way round, so the whole assembly is written backwards
to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
the Tamils are a people of Sri Lanka

explanation.surface: The mood in London's financial district, keeping a Sri Lankan employee in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The City, capitalised, is London's financial district; 'back' applies to the whole assembly, not just the Sri Lankan.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate can mean the prevailing mood or conditions, as in 'the economic climate', matching atmosphere in its figurative sense.

clue.text: Start to train, going off jogging

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word
food going off is rotting

explanation.surface: Begin your fitness training by setting out for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' looks like departing, but it means decaying, as food does.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotting and jogging both describe running at a slow, steady pace, so they serve as everyday synonyms.

clue.text: One seeing future friend on film

indicators.note: in a down answer, one part sitting on another comes above it, so it is read first

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a film of moisture is a mist

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a future friend appearing in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie but is a thin layer, here of mist; 'future friend' is a false pairing across the definition boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmist reads people's hands to tell fortunes, claiming to see what lies ahead for them.

clue.text: A key instrument, mostly for dealing with bees

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a piano is an instrument played with keys

explanation.surface: An important musical tool, used mainly for handling bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important, but it describes the piano's keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Apian is the adjective relating to bees, from Latin apis, so it covers anything concerning them.

clue.text: Be idle, mostly, in quiet areas, on vacation in city squares

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, between its outer parts

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: a vacated place has been emptied, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to laze is to be idle

explanation.surface: On holiday, idling mostly in calm spots within the town's open spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' reads as being on holiday but means emptied of its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public open square in a town or city, from the Spanish word, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Horse might don this headgear, with rain so bad

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear

indicators.note: bad means faulty or wrong, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse might wear a hat when the weather is foul.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: what a horse might wear. 'Headgear' tempts as the definition but only gives CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth covering spread over a horse's saddle and harness, worn on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Group in Arctic senses dropping temperature

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to intuit is to sense something without reasoning
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: Arctic explorers sense the temperature falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senses' is a verb here, giving INTUITS, which loses one of its two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are an indigenous people of the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland and Alaska, a population group there.

clue.text: Figure welcoming a vote, revolutionary US statesperson

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the letters are read the other way
to welcome someone is to let them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a net figure is the amount left after deductions
taken as written
a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A figure welcoming the ballot of a radical American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesperson' looks like a politician, but it means a person from a US state; NET takes in A and X, then turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Texan is a native or resident of Texas, so quite literally a person from one American state.

clue.text: Appealing dancer aroused males, inspiring love

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside another
aroused means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An alluring dancer excites the men watching and inspires their passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appealing' is a pun: Salome danced to appeal to Herod and won her request for John the Baptist's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Salome is the biblical figure whose dance of the seven veils so pleased Herod that he granted her wish.

clue.text: Worthless person taken in by low bloodsucker

indicators.note: something taken in by another is absorbed inside it, so it is enclosed

parts.note: cattle low, that is, moo
squit is British slang for a small, insignificant person

explanation.surface: A good-for-nothing is conned by a despicable parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as an adjective meaning base, but it is the verb for the noise a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Female mosquitoes feed on the blood of animals and people, so they are literal bloodsucking insects.

clue.text: What 1, 9, 10, 11, 12, 17, 20, 22, 25 and 26 all have is a moral failing once

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split differently: each of those answers has a capital city in it
second meaning: an old term for one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: The listed answers share a feature, which is also a bygone kind of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as CAPITALS IN: IRRIGATE holds RIGA, then BERLIN, BERN, OSLO, ROME, LIMA, APIA, PARIS, LOME and QUITO in the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital sin is the older name for a deadly sin such as pride or greed, a grave moral fault in Christian teaching.

clue.text: In which you may see swimmers fail

definitions.text: In which you may see swimmers
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a container of water, such as one for fish
second meaning: informal verb for flopping badly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmers' suggests a pool and people, but think of fish in an aquarium.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish tank holds swimming fish, and a show or business that tanks fails badly, an informal sense.
